clue.text: Prime minister happy to put on weight

parts.note: happy means glad
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A cheerful premier who doesn't mind gaining a few pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put on' is a link joining the two pieces; William Gladstone was a Victorian British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone served four terms as Britain's Liberal premier in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Irish water-ghoul in strange form

indicators.note: letters shown in a strange form are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A monster lurking in an Irish lake looks oddly shaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in strange form' rearranges GHOUL; a lough is the Irish spelling of a lake or sea inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ireland a lake or sea inlet is called by this Gaelic-derived word, like Scottish loch.

clue.text: Fitting church into hollow

indicators.note: one piece is put into another, so CE goes inside

parts.note: a dent is a hollow
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Installing a church in a valley seems appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is the container signal; 'Fitting' reads like a noun for a fixture but is the adjective meaning proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something proper or seemly for an occasion.

clue.text: Tawdry art put up and reserved

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up means reading it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a reserved person is shy

explanation.surface: Cheap artwork hung on the wall, kept back for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ART into TRA in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap, showy and of poor quality: synonyms for gaudy rubbish.

clue.text: Pins that are filed away

definitions.meaning: small metal fasteners hammered into wood
fingernails are shaped with a nail file

explanation.definitionFit: Metal fasteners driven in with a hammer, and the horny tips of fingers that people file down.

clue.text: All out to see senior officer's three-wheeler?

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer, with the possessive giving the S
a trike is a tricycle, with three wheels

explanation.surface: Everyone turns out to watch a top brass officer's tricycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see' is a link. 'All out' is a union call for everyone to stop work.
explanation.definitionFit: When a union calls everyone out, workers across all industries stop work together.

clue.text: Change of thin, crude, long combinations etc.

indicators.note: a change of these words means altering the order of their letters

explanation.surface: Swapping thin, rough, long-legged woollens for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of' rearranges THIN, CRUDE and LONG. Combinations are an old one-piece undergarment covering body and legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Combinations were a one-piece vest-and-long-johns garment worn beneath outer clothes.

clue.text: Acted in unison, perhaps, to make public accusations

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be put in another order

explanation.surface: People behaving in concert so as to make allegations openly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ACTED IN UNISON; 'to make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Open condemnations of someone, made publicly, are formal charges or accusations.

clue.text: It is usually marked on the ground

definitions.text: It is usually marked on the ground

parts.words: It is usually marked on the ground
parts.note: a cricket ground, where a record card of runs is filled in during play, not a mark on the turf

explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' suggests the earth, but means a sports ground where the card of runs and wickets is filled in.
explanation.definitionFit: A card on which runs, wickets or golf strokes are recorded as play goes on.

clue.text: Sad imperial polygamist, perhaps?

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad
an imperial is a small pointed beard below the lower lip

explanation.surface: A gloomy emperor with many wives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imperial' looks like a word for an emperor, but is a style of beard. Bluebeard is the folk-tale man who murdered his successive wives.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk-tale villain married wife after wife, killing each one, so he serves as an example of a serial husband.

clue.text: Bohemian bank-draft in statement?

indicators.note: a statement is something spoken, so the word is heard not seen

parts.note: a cheque is a bank draft ordering payment

explanation.surface: An artistic type uses a cheque for a bank statement.
explanation.walkthrough: Bohemia is a region of the Czech Republic, so 'Bohemian' is not the artistic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia forms the western part of the Czech Republic, so its natives are its nationals.

clue.text: Appropriate lift?

definitions.meaning: used as a verb, to take for oneself without right
informal for to pinch or pilfer

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to take something belonging to another without permission.

clue.text: Hangs around for reinforcements

definitions.meaning: lingers or remains in a place
supports such as the stiffening strips of a corset or ropes bracing a mast

explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to remain, and corset bones or ship ropes are supports that strengthen.

clue.text: Short drink-kind to take about noon

indicators.note: the first piece takes the second about, wrapping round it

parts.note: a kind is a sort

explanation.surface: Someone having a quick tipple around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take about' puts N inside SORT; a snort is a quick nip of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tot of spirits knocked back quickly is informally called this.

clue.text: End encased in gold for so long

indicators.note: one piece is encased in another, going inside it

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
to end, as a life, is to die

explanation.surface: Death wrapped in gold as a farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encased in' is the container signal and 'for' a link; 'End' is the verb, to die, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are farewells said on parting, French goodbye and casual English leave-taking.

clue.text: Wet slapping sound that backs the chair

definitions.meaning: the noise of something soggy hitting a surface
a central upright piece forming the back of a chair

explanation.definitionFit: The noise a soggy object makes landing, and the flat central upright in a chair's back.

clue.text: Mind goal

definitions.meaning: sanity or the power of thought, as in losing one's wits
a purpose or motive for doing something

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is rational thought or sanity, the other the purpose behind an action.

clue.text: Essential nature of gypsy cheerfulness

indicators.note: the answer is formed of letters inside these two words

explanation.surface: The true spirit of a traveller's good humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' points to the run inside 'gypsy cheerfulness'.
explanation.definitionFit: The soul or inner self is a person's deepest character.

clue.text: Bay window in college

definitions.meaning: a window projecting from an upper floor

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A projecting upper-storey window, and the name of an Oxford University college.

clue.text: Truces arranged too late for him in Montana?

indicators.note: letters arranged are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Peace deals came too late for a general in Montana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges TRUCES; 'too late for' is a link. George Custer died at the Little Bighorn in Montana in 1876.
explanation.definitionFit: The US cavalry general was killed with his men at the Battle of the Little Bighorn, Montana.

clue.text: A Trollope character not on the level

parts.note: Obadiah Slope is the scheming chaplain in Barchester Towers by Anthony Trollope

explanation.surface: A Victorian novelist's figure is a bit shady.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian English novelist. 'not on the level' suggests dishonesty but means tilted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on a slant or incline is not flat or horizontal.

clue.text: Hope for conviction

definitions.meaning: used as a verb, to have confidence in or rely on

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses involve confident belief: to rely hopefully, and faith or certainty.

clue.text: One poor at games needs time under teacher

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece under another comes after it

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

explanation.surface: A weak sportsman needs extra coaching time.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a rabbit is a poor player, especially a weak batsman in cricket or a duffer at tennis. 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: British sporting slang for an inept player, especially a tail-end batsman in cricket.

clue.text: Fights for titbits

explanation.definitionFit: Brawls or squabbles, and small leftover fragments of food.

clue.text: Head of Russian river in the country

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the Ural is a river flowing from Russia into the Caspian Sea

explanation.surface: A Russian river source in rustic surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' takes R from 'Russian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing life away from towns, in farmland and villages.

clue.text: Wood-worker makes strip of wood come to a point

indicators.note: the strip comes to the point, so the letter is joined on after it

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A carpenter sharpens a slat into a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood-worker' suggests a carpenter, but is a machine that turns wood. 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning machine shapes timber by spinning it against a cutting tool.

clue.text: Number in theatre? Three, roughly

indicators.note: roughly signals the letters are a loose rearrangement

explanation.surface: Counting the people in a playhouse comes to about three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is read as something that numbs, an anaesthetic in an operating theatre. 'roughly' rearranges THREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A once-common anaesthetic that deadens feeling in a surgical operating room.

clue.text: Tree which has many rings, presumably

definitions.meaning: a small tree bearing white flowers and dark berries
an older tree has more growth rings in its trunk

explanation.definitionFit: A shrub bearing flowers and berries, and one more aged, as tree rings count years.

clue.text: Blade entering ship is fun for kids

parts.note: a skate is a boot with a blade
boarding is going onto a ship

explanation.surface: A sword-wielding pirate climbing onto a vessel enjoys himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blade' suggests a sword, but is an ice skate. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a wheeled plank is a popular pastime among children.

clue.text: Making impression is attempt at such work

parts.note: a dent is an impression made in a surface
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Leaving a mark is a stab at the dental profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' and 'at' are links; 'such work' looks back to the making of impressions, as dentists take moulds of teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentists take moulds of teeth, so making impressions is part of their profession.
